A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same causal-minimality research. All 35 pages of v1 and 28 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable and support comparison. Removed language-model material can be distinguished from relocated vision material.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices B.3 and F report original diffusion-model unlearning, editing and sparsity experiments, plus Gemma language-model concept graphs.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E retain original Stable Diffusion and Flux experiments, including quantitative unlearning, editing and sparsity results.

M1.justification: v2 removes the complete language-specific adaptation in v1 Appendices B.3 and E: pretrained Gemma SAEs applied to sequential token segments and different layers, followed by PC discovery of textual hierarchies. The retained diffusion pipeline of sparse SAEs, cross-timestep causal discovery and feature steering is unchanged.

E1.justification: The Gemma-2-2b-it experiments on pile-10k disappear, eliminating evaluated language-domain coverage. The image-generation, nudity/style unlearning and editing tasks remain, with the same vision datasets.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5, including ConceptSteer, SAE without hierarchy and the style-removal baselines. The deleted language case studies did not contain a separate baseline comparison.

E3.justification: The language experiment's protocol is removed, including padding exclusion and assignment of three token segments to SAEs at layers 18, 19 and 20. Retained vision settings, sample counts, metrics and budgets are unchanged. Figure 4's added K labels restate settings already documented in v1.

E4.justification: The language case studies examining humor/legal terminology and emphasis/yell-mode hierarchies in v1 Figures 8 and 15 are removed. Vision timestep analyses, sparsity ablations and editing case studies remain; the revised sparsity figure does not introduce a new experiment.

E5.justification: Tables 3 and 6 retain identical uncertainty summaries. Table 6 still specifies 100 panda images generated using different random seeds. No repeated-run, confidence-interval or significance-testing practice changes.

E6.justification: The qualitative Gemma findings about humor, pronouns, legal terminology and yell-mode relationships are removed. All numerical entries in Tables 1-6 are unchanged, including the proposed method's Table 1 I2P value of 0.25 and P4D value of 0.66. Retained vision findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 removes the discrete textual formulation, Condition B.1, Theorem B.2 and its Appendix C.2 proof, including the nonnegative-rank and state-equivalence arguments. Continuous Condition 4.2, Theorem 4.3 and their proof remain, with the proof relocated from Appendix C.1 to B.1.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the contribution from vision and autoregressive language models, with continuous and discrete identifiability, to continuous hierarchical selection models and text-to-image experiments. However, Section 2 still retains the broader claim of identifiability for both continuous and discrete models.

C2.justification: The substantive explanation connecting growing language context, state compression and increasingly abstract textual concepts is removed. The assumptions discussion also loses its language-compressibility rationale and cross-modal validation argument. Vision interpretations remain; the conclusion adds an explicit statement that broader misspecification guarantees remain future work.

D1.justification: The language reproducibility information is removed, including pretrained Gemma-Scope SAEs, pile-10k processing and layer assignments. Vision hyperparameters, Flux implementation details, L40/M1 hardware information and approximately eight-hour SAE training time remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Eight references associated with the deleted language branch are removed, including SAELens, Pile, Gemma, the two Kivva papers and the compression/nonnegative-rank references. Most related-work discussion remains unchanged, while the introduction narrows the novelty claim to continuous models.

P1.justification: The retained text receives targeted edits: language-model references are pruned, the timestep explanation and proof-sketch cross-reference are corrected, a limitations paragraph is added, and one affiliation changes. Main section order and most prose remain; surviving appendices are renumbered after the language appendix and proof are deleted.

P2.justification: The visual account changes from two modalities to vision only: v1's language Figures 7, 8 and 15 disappear, Figure 1 loses its LLM-compression component, and the dual-modality method diagram becomes the enlarged vision-only Figure 7 in v2. Figure 4 gains explicit K labels, and Table 6 is relocated without changing its contents.

improvement.justification: Clearer sparsity labels, corrected explanations and explicit limitations provide modest benefits. However, v2 removes the discrete-identifiability theorem and proof while Section 2 still claims that result, creating a claim-evidence inconsistency that v1 did not have. With the retained vision theory and numerical evidence unchanged, this supports a limited overall decline rather than a penalty for narrowing scope itself.
